text:
Devon: Heads up — seeing intermittent packet loss and 200ms+ spikes between pods in gpu-pool-4 (cross-node) but only over IPv6. IPv4 paths look fine.
Alex: Is this new? Any recent calico/kube-proxy changes in us-west-2?
Devon: We rolled calico 3.25 -> 3.26 last night (BPF dataplane) and kube-proxy switched to IPVS for svc by canary. Impact started ~01:12 UTC.
Iasha: Can you paste ip -6 route and ip link from one of the affected nodes? Also any RDMA pods affected or just TCP?
Devon: RDMA jobs (RoCEv2) hitting errors too — high retransmits and huge tail latency. Quick outputs:
```
Devon@node-a:~$ ip -6 route show
fe80::/64 dev eth0 proto kernel metric 256 pref medium
2001:db8:10::/64 via fe80::1 dev eth0 proto static
::/0 dev vxlan.calico scope link
```
```
Devon@node-a:~$ ip link show eth0
4: eth0: mtu 9000 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
```
```
Devon@node-b:~$ ip -6 route show
::/0 via fe80::2 dev eth0 proto static
2001:db8:10::/64 dev vxlan.calico proto kernel metric 1024
```
Irene: Hmm, asymmetric IPv6 default route — node-a sends via overlay, node-b uses native ToR. Possible MTU mismatch on IPv6 path.
Alex: Any kernel logs showing PMTU blackhole or fragmentation? Can you run tcpdump for UDP/rocev2 and icmp6?
Devon: tcpdump showed lots of "Fragmentation needed and DF set" ICMPv6 on the path where the overlay->ToR translation happens.
netbot: Alert: ToR config change detected in us-west-2a at 01:10 UTC — IPv6 jumbo frames disabled on leaf-03. (change_id: cfg-7861)
sre-bot: Incident ticket #INC-2026-348 created and linked.
Iasha: That explains it — RoCEv2 uses UDP encapsulation and is sensitive to MTU; fragmented UDP can get dropped by some switches or TOE. Calico overlay default MTU set to 1440 by BPF path; eth0 is 9000 on some nodes, ToR now 1500 for IPv6, so IPv6 traffic gets forced onto smaller path and plus asymmetry means reply path prefers a different MTU.
Irene: Quick mitigations: 1) pin RDMA/GPU workloads to nodes with consistent IPv6 path (taint/affinity), 2) set calico.nodeMTU to 1500 across affected nodes, 3) rollback calico BPF change if it keeps preferring overlay for IPv6.
Alex: Agreed. Also as short-term workaround we can prefer IPv4 for intra-pod RDMA by setting pod-level netpolicy to prefer v4 endpoints or update service annotations to prefer IPv4 endpoints for the critical svc.
Devon: Applying calico.nodeMTU=1500 to the DaemonSet now (rolling parallel to 5 nodes). Starting on node-b -> node-f.
Iasha: While rolling, run these checks on each node as it comes back:
```
# verify routes and mtu
ip -6 route show default
ip link show eth0
ethtool -k eth0 | grep tx-checksumming
# quick ipv6 perf
kubectl exec -n gpu nsenter -- iperf3 -6 -c <peer-pod-ipv6> -t 10
```
Devon: Patching complete on 6/6 nodes in us-west-2a. Early results: RTTs back to ~1-2ms, no more icmp6 PMTU logs. RDMA jobs resumed normally.
Irene: Follow-ups: 1) Confirm ToR IPv6 MTU config across all racks, 2) add a preflight in calico rollout to detect ToR MTU mismatches, 3) add an alert for asymmetric IPv6 default routes.
Alex: I'll own the preflight change and ToR audit. Devon/Iasha please run a subset of RDMA regression tests in staging with BPF enabled before next canary.
Devon: On it — kicking off tests now. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Iasha: Filing follow-up doc with commands and mitigation steps in #eng-infra runbook.
netbot: INC-2026-348 updated: root cause identified as "ToR IPv6 MTU rollback + overlay route asymmetry during calico BPF rollout".
